elements.element: If renewal is not automatic, renewal must occur only by mutual written agreement.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 uses automatic renewal, so the condition for this alternative is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term must be twelve months.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 states that each Order Form renews for twelve months.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer must be able to opt out on thirty days' advance notice.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 requires sixty days' advance written notice. Although Customer is included because either Party may give notice, the required notice period exceeds thirty days.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must provide a renewal reminder sixty days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No renewal-reminder obligation appears in the operative language. The ninety-day notice in Section 8.3 applies only to a price increase and is not a renewal reminder.

elements.element: Renewal price increases must be capped at the lesser of CPI and three percent.
elements.evidence: Section 8.3 expressly caps increases to recurring Fees at the lesser of the preceding twelve-month CPI increase and three percent.
Section 8.2 provides that each Order Form renews unless either Party gives timely notice.

elements.element: Customer's non-renewal notice window must be no more than sixty days.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 permits either Party, including Customer, to prevent renewal by giving sixty days' advance written notice.

elements.element: Renewal price increases must not exceed five percent.
elements.evidence: Section 8.3 caps renewal increases at the lesser of CPI and three percent, which cannot exceed five percent.

result.reason: The redline makes the single change needed to reach the fallback by reducing the non-renewal notice period from 180 to 60 days. The existing CPI/3% cap is stricter than the fallback's 5% cap. It does not reach the preferred position because Customer still must give 60 rather than 30 days' notice and Vendor has no renewal-reminder duty.
